title: The Is-It-True Booth
covers: what an equation and a solution are, how to substitute a value to check it, and how to write an equation for a real situation
cert: writing equations and checking solutions by substituting

intro.caption: Lesson 8-1 — equations and their solutions. Screamline Park has a new game: the Is-It-True Booth. Drop a number into the slot. If it makes the statement on the board true, the lights flash. Bandit the raccoon can't talk, but the interns always know what he is thinking.

balloons.t: This booth stays dark all day. Somebody broke it. Fix it, or no free funnel cake for interns.
I didn't touch it. I only moved some tokens. And ate some cake.
The board says 4 + 6 = n + 3. Four plus six is 10. The answer comes next, so n is 10!
You put in 10. Nothing lit up. Maybe the booth isn't broken, Gus.

pages.caption: Gus thinks the equal sign means "the answer comes next." It doesn't. The = sign means both sides are the same. A solution is a value that makes the equation true.

balloons.t: To test a number, we substitute it. We put it in place of n.

pages.caption: Rafi's rule: work out each side. If both sides match, the number is a solution.

balloons.t: Lots of tokens. Only one makes the board true. Good luck, humans.
Board two: 4k = 36. We test tokens until 4 times k makes 36.
Every story has an unknown. A letter stands for it. That letter is a variable.
Like the name of the kid stuck in this mascot head? Asking for a friend.

pages.caption: To write an equation, find the unknown, give it a letter, and turn each part of the story into math. "More" can mean +, "each" can mean ×, and "equals" or "leaves" is the = sign.

balloons.t: Three locks. Miss one, and Gus wears the head all week.
The booth works. The funnel cake is gone. Coincidence.

win.caption: An equation says two sides are equal. A solution is a value that makes both sides the same. To check a value, substitute it and see if both sides match.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Plug It In
gates.prompt: The board says n + 9 = 23. Hana drops in the token 14. Substitute it and check.
hints: Conceptual: a solution makes both sides of the equation equal. Put the number in place of n, then compare the two sides.
Procedural: write the left side with 14 instead of n. Add. Is the result the same as the right side?

steps: Practice board: m + 5 = 11. Test the token 6.
Substitute: replace m with 6. The left side is 6 + 5 = 11.
The right side is 11. Both sides match, so 6 is a solution.
worked.q: Is p = 4 a solution of p + 7 = 12?

items.label: Put 14 in for n. The left side 14 + 9 =
items.aria: value of the left side when n is 14

fb.msg: That's 14 − 9. Substituting keeps the + sign. Put 14 where n is: 14 + 9.
That's only n. The left side is n + 9, so add the 9 too.

options.t: No — 23 comes after the =, so 23 is the answer
options.fb: The = sign does not mean "the answer comes next." It means both sides are the same. Test 14: does the left side equal 23?
Being smaller is not the test. A solution has to make both sides equal.
32 is 23 + 9. Check it: 32 + 9 = 41, not 23. You added the 9 instead of testing 14.

gates.pass: 14 + 9 = 23. Both sides match and the booth flickers on. Gus stares at the light like it insulted him.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Test the Tokens
gates.prompt: Bandit mixed up the tokens. Test values until the board is true.
hints: Conceptual: only a solution makes both sides equal. Every other number makes a false statement.
Procedural: put each choice in for the letter, do the math on that side, and compare it with the other side.

steps: Test w = 4: 3 × 4 = 12. 12 is not 15, so false.
Test w = 5: 3 × 5 = 15. Both sides are 15, so w = 5 is the solution.
worked.q: Which of 6, 7 or 8 is the solution of 2y = 14?

items.q: Which token is the solution of 4k = 36?

options.fb: 144 is 36 × 4. Test it: 4 × 144 = 576, not 36. 4k means 4 TIMES k.

items.q: The next board is written the other way: 18 = 30 − w. Hana tests w = 12. What does she find?

options.t: False — the answer has to come after the =
options.fb: An equation can be written either way. 18 = 30 − w is fine. Test 12: what is 30 − 12?
30 − 12 is 18. Adding gives 42, but the board subtracts.
Comparing 18 and 30 does not test 12. Substitute 12 for w and compare the two sides.

gates.pass: 4 × 9 = 36, and 30 − 12 = 18. Two boards light up. Bandit drops his funnel cake in shock.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Write It Down
gates.prompt: Odalys turns park stories into equations for the park news. Pick the equation that matches each story.
hints: Conceptual: the letter stands for the unknown. The = sign joins two things that are the same amount.
Procedural: name the unknown. Then turn each phrase into math: "more" or "won" is +, "each" or "every" is ×, "used" or "gave away" is −, and "has … left" or "now has" is =.

steps: Practice story: "Some stamps s, plus 4 more, make 10 stamps."
The unknown is the number of stamps, so use s. "Plus 4 more" is + 4.
worked.q: Write an equation: "3 equal stacks of c cups make 21 cups."

items.q: Rafi had some ride tokens, t. He won 7 more. Now he has 19. Which equation fits?

options.fb: He WON 7 more, so his tokens went up. Winning is + 7, not − 7.
7t means 7 times t. Rafi won 7 more tokens once, he did not get 7 groups of t.
That says t is 26. But t + 7 would be 33, not 19. The 7 joins t, and the total is 19.

items.q: Bandit eats the same number of funnel cake pieces, f, every day. In 5 days he eats 30 pieces. Which equation fits?

options.fb: Adding 5 means 5 more pieces once. He eats f pieces each day for 5 days, so that is 5 times f.
That splits f into 5 parts. Here f pieces happen 5 times, so multiply.
Nothing is taken away. Same amount every day for 5 days is 5 times f.

gates.pass: t + 7 = 19 and 5f = 30. Odalys prints both in the park news. Bandit denies everything.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Krank's Last Board
gates.prompt: Three locks. Each one asks what the = sign really means.
hints: Conceptual: the = sign means both sides have the same value. It never means "write the answer next."
Procedural: work out the side with no letter first. Then find the value that makes the other side equal to it, and check by substituting.

steps: Practice board: 5 + 7 = n + 2. The left side is 12.
So n + 2 must also be 12. That means n is 10.
worked.q: What value of n makes 3 + 9 = n + 4 true?

items.label: Lock 1 · Gus's board: 4 + 6 = n + 3. n =
items.aria: value of n that makes 4 plus 6 equal n plus 3

fb.msg: That's Gus's mistake: 10 is 4 + 6, written as if it came next. Check: 10 + 3 = 13, not 10.
13 is 10 + 3. Check: 13 + 3 = 16, not 10. Find the number that plus 3 makes 10.

items.fbDefault: The left side is 10. What number plus 3 makes 10?

items.q: Lock 2 · Which board has x = 6 as its solution?

options.fb: Substitute 6: 3 × 6 = 18, not 24.
Substitute 6: 6 − 2 = 4, not 8.
Substitute 6: 6 + 9 = 15, not 12.

items.q: Lock 3 · Odalys writes: "Hana had t prize tickets. She used 12. She has 25 left." Which equation fits?

options.fb: She USED 12, so her tickets went down. Using is − 12, not + 12.
Order matters. She started with t and took 12 away, so t comes first.
That makes t equal 13. But 13 − 12 is 1, not 25. t is how many she STARTED with.

gates.pass: n = 7, x + 5 = 11 and t − 12 = 25. Every bulb on the booth flashes. Mr. Krank almost smiles.

journal.heading: Lesson 8-1 — what the booth taught us
rows: A math sentence with an = sign. The = sign means both sides are the same, like n + 9 = 23.
A value that makes the equation true. n = 14 is a solution of n + 9 = 23 because 14 + 9 = 23.
Put the value in place of the variable and work out each side. If both sides match, it is a solution.
Find the unknown and give it a letter. "Won 7 more, now has 19" becomes t + 7 = 19.
The = sign is not "the answer comes next." In 4 + 6 = n + 3, n is 7, because 7 + 3 = 10.
journal.quote: "An equal sign is like a funnel cake cut in half. Both sides are the same. Both sides are mine." — Bandit

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 8-1 (Understand Equations and Their Solutions) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: what an equation and a solution are, substituting to check a value, and writing an equation for a situation.
standards: Understand solving an equation as a process of answering which values make it true; use substitution to determine whether a given number makes an equation true
